newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up but trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up but trade quiet.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week higher, but trade was quiet with no news of fresh interest, save for some inquiries on SMR grades, traders said.
At the close, June RSS1 buyer was officially quoted at 285 Malaysian/Singapore cents ($1.13) a kg, up one cent from Tuesday. June SMR20 was also one cent higher at 266.
Dealing houses quoted SMR CV at 332 cents, SMR L at 310, SMR 10 at 264 and drum latex at 229.
Sustained overseas coupled with local dealers shortcovering, in view of the upcoming summer holiday, should push up Malaysian rubber prices next week, dealers said.
"The summer holiday is approaching soon and many Europeans are seen building up their stocks ahead of the vacation," a dealer said.
The INRO five-day average was 214.09 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 29 from 213.60 on May 28. The daily indicator was 215.15 against 214.83.
A Malaysia-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU (or 20-ft container), and $1,700 per two-TEU containers (or 40-ft container).
